We searched the addresses
of the Docent's accomplices.
The helmet wasn't there.
436:
That leaves one lead:
Prokhorov, the cloakroom attendant.
437:
But we couldn't pursue it.
Prokhorov didn't turn up for the meeting.
438:
He may have suspected something.
He quit his job and hasn't gone home.
440:
You have our deepest apologies
and enormous thanks.
Take off the wig, wash off the tattoos,
441:
go home and celebrate New Year's.
Thank you very much.
- What about my men?
442:
We'll return your charges
to prison today.
443:
What if the cloakroom attendant
turns up? Could you need us again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you, but Bely,
the Docent, escaped from the prison camp today.
445:
It's incredible, but true.
It's dangerous for you to look like him.
446:
Could we wait until tomorrow?
It is New Year's, and they did try,
in their own way.
447:
We're outside the city.
The Docent's unlikely to find us.
448:
All right, but don't leave the dacha!
Oh, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife.
Here's her reply, addressed to him.
450:
- Promise you'll have dinner with us on New Year's Day?
- We promise!
451:
What a shame. Such a nice woman,
and her father's a fence.
452:
Why all the shouting? Who said you could go out?
- Here he is... The bad person.
454:
The New Year is here. I hope
it brings each of you a new beginning.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
Wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you,
and I'll find you. I promise.
457:
- And now... just a moment...
- Where's he off to?
458:
Who knows?
You can't make sense of him anymore.
459:
What's to make sense of?
He says he'll find us wherever we are
and slit our throats.
461:
They say he went like this
across Speckle's throat with a razor.
- He's gone completely savage, the jackal.
462:
Who's come to visit?
Father Frost, with presents for you!
463:
- Come here, Fedya. - What did I do?
- Come on. Wear these in good health. Hand-knitted.
464:
- What do I need them for? I don't even have a home.
- You will. Your whole life's ahead of you.
465:
- You can use them in prison for now. Wear them.
- You always have to jinx it.
466:
This is for you, Vasya...
And this is for you, Gavrila Petrovich.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you, too.
469:
Sour stuff.
It's boring without vodka.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could sit and talk.
Have a real heart-to-heart.
472:
I'm not a prosecutor. I'm not having
a heart-to-heart with you.
- We could play a game.
473:
Listen to him! Think I'm some sucker
who'd play you? You've got nine aces
in that deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow."
476:
You name a city beginning with the last
letter, W: Warsaw. Then you say one
beginning with W. Understand?
477: Now you, Fedya. A city beginning with W.
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- Fine. Yours begins with A.
- Dzhambul. - Why Dzhambul?
480:
Because it's warm there.
It's my home. My mother lives there.
481:
Let's try this game instead.
I'll go out, you hide something,
then I'll come back and find it.
482:
- You'd do better finding our helmet.
- Quiet.
483:
- We'll hide something, and he'll peek through a hole?
- Of course not. You go out and hide.
484:
And you make sure I don't peek.
Why me? Every time, it's Fedya.
485:
- I'll rip your mouth off, you little scoundrel!
- My mouth, my mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- Yes.
487:
- Did you have a father and mother?
- Yes.
488:
Why are you so mean?
Why are you like a dog?
490:
- You came on your own.
- Oh, you're here too.
491:
I was about to come to your place,
but I sensed a trap.
492: Mityai, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Keep walking.
495:
- Sorry to trouble you for nothing, doctor.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea
and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It does, Vasya. Read it.
499:
"Dear Dad, we learned
that you're in prison,
500:
and we were very happy,
because we thought you were dead."
501:
Who told that little squirt
about Gloomy?
502:
"Mom was happy too, because when
your letter came, she cried all day.
503:
Before, she told us you were
a test pilot."
505:
"But I'm glad you're alive anyway,
because Mom says
506:
you're a good person,
but weak-willed."
507:
Right! Weak-willed. You swiped
our money and blamed the taxi driver.
508: Get lost! I'll knock your horns off, rat!
510:
Aren't you ashamed?
You're forty years old. Half your lives
are already behind you.
511:
What have you done with them?
What do you have now? What lies ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, not a shred of decency!
Come to your senses before it's too late.
That's my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we need to get out.
The doctor will tip off the police.
514:
- She won't. - Why not?
- I slit her throat with a razor...
515:
She's down the well.
Go and look if you want.
516:
What was my sentence?
One year.
517:
How much will I get for escaping?
Three years!
518:
How much for the kindergarten
and the apartment? Say ten!
520:
So I'm supposed to put up with
that snake just to avoid
a lousy fourteen years?
521:
The one who put the old lady in the well?
Do what you want. I'm going to the police.
522: Go on! He won't touch you.
523:
And you two?
You'll put up with him until he kills you?
524:
Vasya, I told him earlier
that I had a cold, and he...
525:
Enough about your cold.
Come here...
527:
- What are you doing?
- Cleaning the carpet.
528:
Listen, comrades. The comedy's over.
First, I'll take this off.
530:
I'll serve my time, and that's it.
I'll go straight! Get a job.
531:
- Doing what? Night watchman at my old collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I could shovel snow, lay bricks,
or be a translator. I know English.
533:
If only we'd brought the hat!
Who's the Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are plenty of crooks, but only one hat.
- They'd reduce our sentences for the helmet.
535:
Where did he put it?
We went everywhere.
536:
Crook! Remember when I said
I had a cold? And you threatened
to rip my mouth off.
537:
- You made me dive in that freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When they caught us. Remember?
He said, "I'm fishing," then told you to dive.
539:
- Wait. What did he say about fishing?
- "I'm fishing through the ice."
540:
- Then, "Squint, can you swim?"
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole!
541:
That's right! I remember now, the rat!
It's in the ice hole at Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn't you say so, you blockhead?
Could've left us a note when you hanged yourself.
- Come on.
543:
- What about him?
- Leave him. They can pick him up. I'm not carrying that ox. Come on!
545:
- There's nothing down there.
- It is. At the bottom. You'll have to dive.
546:
Why me? Every time, it's Squint.
Vasya, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can't! It's cold. I'll get sick.
548:
- A minute ago you were hanging yourself, and now you fear a cold!
- Keep fit, everyone!
550:
- Where's the boat station?
- Over there.
551:
I'd kill you both,
but I haven't got time!
552:
Now there are two of them.
And another one at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich! Well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we turn in, the better.
